messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGING: SLO breach detected for model-redwood-13b-int8 in prod-us-west-2. Alert INC-2026-0345. p95=320ms (SLO 200ms), p99=980ms (SLO 500ms). Streaming stalls reported (partial/empty chunks). On-call: @sara_ml

sara_ml: looking. grabbing traces and tail logs now. any recent rollouts to int8 quant profiles?

mike_infra: yes — there was a quant-profile push at 2026-06-12T04:10:05Z to the prod-west pool (rollout id rp-9482). Canary passed but full rollout started at 04:12 UTC. seeing a correlation with p99 spikes.

juan_ml: logs show dequant errors and KV-cache misses spiking. suspect calibration fallout from new int8 profile -> dequant path thrashing KV cache and blocking stream flush.

ashley_cs: we have 2 customers (ACME, BrightApp) opening support tickets complaining about stalled streaming responses. ACME flagged as high priority.

samir_ops: tagging metrics: CPU spiking on inference nodes + model runtime threads blocked. attaching quick snapshot:

```
{
  "model": "redwood-13b-int8",
  "rollout_id": "rp-9482",
  "deployed_at": "2026-06-12T04:12:05Z",
  "p95_ms": 320,
  "p99_ms": 980,
  "streaming_stalls": 47
}
```

incident-bot: recommended playbooks: fallback-to-fp16-variant, rollback-quant-profile, increase-concurrency-pool.

sara_ml: doing ordered mitigations — 1) pause rollout, 2) rollback profile to rp-9460 (last-known-good), 3) if that doesn't stabilize, shift traffic to redwood-13b-fp16 variant for streaming clients.

mike_infra: on it. pausing rollout in deployment manager... pause applied.

mike_infra: initiating rollback to rp-9460 on pool prod-west-quant. will drain new workers (no kill) and bring up nodes with rp-9460. ETA ~ 3-5m.

juan_ml: FYI the calibration job that produced rp-9482 showed a higher calibration loss on the 2048-long prompt distribution. suspect quant buckets misaligned -> more dequant ops at runtime. need postmortem.

ashley_cs: messaging CS templates: short notice to affected customers that we're mitigating, ETA 10m, offer temporary capacity bump. I'll send now.

samir_ops: scaling extra fp16 warm nodes just in case. spinning up 4 warm instances in prod-us-west-2 and adding route rule that can shift 20% of streaming sessions if needed.

deploy-bot: RevertAction: rollback rp-9460 applied to pool prod-west-quant by mike_infra at 2026-06-12T04:18:36Z :white_check_mark:

mike_infra: rollback completed on 6/12 04:18:36 UTC. Observability note: KV cache miss-rate and blocking threads dropping. watching p95/p99.

sara_ml: initial numbers post-rollback — p95=180ms, p99=420ms (still slightly over for p99 but much improved). streaming stalls trending down (from 47 -> 6).

juan_ml: still seeing occasional tail spikes aligned with long-context chat sessions. might need a hotfix: guard in runtime to limit dequant concurrency per-request, or prefer fp16 for sessions > 1024 tokens.

ashley_cs: sent update to ACME and BrightApp — they acknowledged, not currently escalating. keeping them in the loop.

samir_ops: shifted 15% of streaming sessions to fp16 pool as precaution. no errors reported on that lane.

sara_ml: handing ops to @mike_infra for infra follow-up; I'll stay on for model debugging and calibration investigation.

mike_infra: taking over. will monitor 30m and then close paging if stable. creating incident ticket INC-2026-0345 in tracker and linking to runbook.

juan_ml: action items: 1) revert/regression test to include tail-latency checks for quant calibration, 2) add pre-release stage that validates long-context workloads at scale, 3) introduce automatic fallback to fp16 when KV-cache miss rate > threshold. I'll open PRs and a postmortem doc.

mike_infra: noted. Ops follow-ups: adjust autoscaler to add short-burst capacity on SLO breach, add alert for streaming-stall > 10 in 5m.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigations applied, major rollback completed, customer impact reduced. Next update planned in 30m or on significant state change.

sara_ml: closing immediate paging — remaining work is post-incident follow-up. thanks everyone for quick triage. :thumbsup:
